name: reflection
context: High-quality generation tasks where a first draft benefits from an explicit critique pass; the same or a second LLM reviews the draft against the goal and a refined version is produced.
benefits: Large quality gains on writing and coding
tradeoffs: Two to three times the token cost
Diminishing returns after two to three cycles
Most tasks plateau at 2 iterations; 3 is hard maximum. Iteration 4 can cause regression
avoid_when: The first attempt is usually sufficient
anti_patterns: Output regression: iteration N+1 is worse than iteration N - track score deltas and revert
Actor and critic seeing each other's chain of reasoning (anchoring bias)
design_principles: Cap cycles at one or two
Use deterministic halt token (e.g., NO_DEFECTS or DONE) for explicit loop termination
Use separate prompts and conversation contexts for actor and critic to prevent anchoring bias
best_practices: Use a different model or temperature for the critic
Stop early on a quality threshold
Consider using a smaller/cheaper model (e.g., Haiku-class) for the critic role
Apply rubric-based critique across defined dimensions: accuracy, completeness, clarity, relevance, safety
Enter revision branch only when critic returns concrete defects; outputs passing on first critique should proceed directly to final output
references: Madaan et al., Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback, NeurIPS 2023 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651
Shinn et al., Reflexion (arxiv:2303.11366) - extends reflection with persistent episodic memory
